The company also expanded its commitment to an open ecosystem by opening up ChatGPT as a shared surface where humans and agents can collaborate and where developers can directly launch new native experiences. There is now a new Pro 500 plan that offers 25 times the ChatGPT Plus allowance and includes access to Ultrafast.

tech.title: Apple's New CEO Seeks to Make Company Run Faster and Leaner
tech.summary: Apple CEO John Ternus is moving to overhaul the company to accelerate product development, broaden its range of devices, and create a leaner organization with a greater focus on engineering. Early ideas under consideration include relying less on traditional spring and fall product release schedules and eliminating some middle-management positions. Ternus has indicated that the company should introduce products more quickly and become more experimental to remain competitive in the AI era. He is seeking new sources of revenue and ways to generate more money from existing products.

tech.title: NASA has a Dragon dilemma, and there appear to be no good answers
tech.summary: SpaceX has made it clear to NASA that it no longer wishes to fly its Crew Dragon spacecraft, or the Falcon 9 rocket, on missions to low-Earth orbit. The company has agreed to support the International Space Station until 2030, but it intends to retire the spacecraft after that. SpaceX has told companies developing private space stations for low-Earth orbit that they cannot order Crew Dragon missions for their habitats. The company has more than fulfilled its contract obligations to NASA, so it is unlikely that the agency can compel SpaceX to keep flying Dragon.

tech.title: Pilotless plane flies over Wichita, putting the future of aviation on display
tech.summary: Joby Aviation recently flew its autonomous aircraft over Wichita. The company has developed a base system that can function in any aircraft. The plane used in the demonstration was a Cessna 208 Caravan that had been retrofitted with Joby's technology. Joby plans to start using the autonomous plane in emergency and cargo transport operations over the next few years, but its end goal is to make it a safe, viable transportation option.

tech.title: Data is the application
tech.summary: AI makes it possible to build faster than ever. However, none of that speed applies to the data. Lose the data that users give you, and you have to start all over again. Let agents iterate over the code, but leave the data to humans.

tech.title: Lemma
tech.summary: Lemma is an open-source workspace where humans and AI agents work as one team. State is shared and permissioned, so many people and many agents work on the same records. It keeps running between sessions, on schedules, webhooks, and table events, and it improves as teams work with it. Lemma can be run locally or on Lemma Cloud.

tech.title: When AI Models Hurt People, the Labs Should Pay

Previous technology waves have shown that industries can survive paying for the harms they cause. One would have to question the societal benefits of an industry if paying for the people it harms or kills is enough to kill the industry.

tech.title: The Case for Meta Enterprise Platform

While the best use of Meta's compute will be its first-party products, an enterprise platform as a 'second' customer makes sense. If Meta underbuilds and can't serve the product it just found product-market fit for, users will drift to competing AI agents/products.

webdev.summary: Agents can generate code. Getting it right for your system is the hard part. You end up wasting time and tokens in the correction loops. webdev.title: How We Built Safety Into Muse
webdev.summary: Muse runs in a dedicated cloud VM where the agent operates inside an isolated runtime cell and never sees real credentials. A separate Sentinel controls connector actions and network egress, while host-side services enforce least privilege, approval scopes, and prompt injection defenses. The design assumes the agent can make mistakes or process hostile data, then limits the damage through layered boundaries and a public bug bounty.

webdev.title: How Our Vibe-Coded Website Looks Like a Designer Made It
webdev.summary: A vibe-coded website became more distinctive when the work shifted from asking an agent for a polished result to building design taste and giving specific visual direction. The process shows how coding agents can make implementation cheap while increasing the value of references, critique, typography, and deliberate constraints.

webdev.title: Language Models for Text Classification: From Bag-of-Words to Jev
webdev.summary: This visual history traces text classification from bag-of-words and recurrent networks through transformers and Jev-style decision APIs. Jev is positioned between narrow specialist classifiers and general-purpose language models, offering broad zero-shot classification with lower latency and cost. The practical opportunity is to use calibrated decision models for routing, screening, evaluation, and other bounded choices inside agent systems.

webdev.title: Getting the Most Out of Opus 5.5
webdev.summary: Give Opus 5.5 a complete task, define what done means, and state when it should stop for input. The model already reasons before every reply, so prompts such as “think carefully” add delay without improving the result. For long coding runs, persistent task files and explicit rules about when to continue help the work survive context compaction and remain steerable.

webdev.title: Data Is the Application
webdev.summary: Agentic coding makes interfaces and features cheap to revise, but user data remains a one-way door that cannot be recreated after a destructive mistake. Schema design, migrations, backups, privacy, and retention therefore deserve slower decisions, explicit recovery plans, and careful validation even when an agent can generate the code in seconds.

webdev.title: A Staff Engineer's Guide to Inventing Work

The goal is to combine strong evidence with leading indicators instead of chasing only the loudest recent problem.

webdev.title: Jev and the Return of the Classifiers

Its “zero hallucination” claim means outputs always fit the supplied schema, not that every decision is correct. The more important promise is calibrated confidence that can route uncertain cases to humans or slower reasoning models, though that calibration requires validation on real workloads.

infosec.title: Official MCP Python SDK Flaw Can Let Malicious Servers Steal OAuth Credentials
infosec.summary: A high-severity flaw in the official MCP Python SDK let malicious MCP servers redirect OAuth token requests to attacker-controlled endpoints. Affected 1.x (1.9.1–1.29.1) and 2.x (2.0.0–2.1.1) clients sent the client secret, authorization code, and PKCE proof key to the attacker, enabling full account takeover with the app's granted permissions. Fixes are in 1.30.0 and 2.2.0. ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider and PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider also require passing issuer= to pin the expected login service.

infosec.title: Automated AI Agent Used to Bread Cybersecurity Nonprofit DIVD

The organization said that the breach was “loud and very, very messy” with the agent working autonomously and over explaining itself in comments, allowing the DIVD to easily reverse-engineer its attack. The threat actor exploited a vulnerability in a vulnerability in an undisclosed software that the organization stated was not Citrix NetScaler.

infosec.title: Pentagon Personnel Agency Data Breach Impacts 3 Million People
infosec.summary: The Defense Manpower Data Center exposed unencrypted personal data through a vulnerable file-sharing server. Unauthorized users accessed files between October 2025 and July 16, 2026. Records included Social Security numbers, names, birth dates, contact details, demographic data, and military specialties. The breach affects 2.76 million living people and 294,000 deceased individuals.

infosec.title: AI Agents Are Privileged Users; Who Is Auditing Their Access?
infosec.summary: Enterprises monitor human logins closely but often grant autonomous AI agents broad production access via long-lived service accounts and API tokens. These agents can initiate, approve, and execute high-value actions end-to-end, collapsing segregation of duties. The piece lays out six controls: isolate agent identities, scope permissions to the minimum needed, assign a business owner, log prompts and tool calls, run periodic access reviews, and build an out-of-band kill switch.

infosec.title: Attackers Abuse ChatGPT Custom GPTs to Deliver RAT via ClickFix
infosec.summary: Sponsored Google results led victims to "Plus 5.6," a Custom GPT on chatgpt.com that answered every prompt with a fake outage notice pointing to a Google Sites ClickFix lure, and Huntress tied at least 40 incidents to the campaign. The eight-stage chain sideloaded malicious DLLs through Canon-signed (later Stardock-signed) binaries, hid its loader inside a WAV file and a NuGet package. It then unpacked a full-featured RAT from a custom encrypted file system that located its C2 over DNS-over-HTTPS. The signed hosts change with each wave, so defenders should detect behaviors instead: PowerShell spawning msiexec on GUID-named MSIs in %TEMP%, signed apps running from fake %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs folders, and self-restoring Run key and scheduled task pairs, which require killing the process before removing persistence.

infosec.title: NeedyMantis: Unpacking a post-compromise malware family used in targeted operations
infosec.summary: NeedyMantis is a modular post-compromise malware family deployed since at least October 2025 by China-based actors, including Storm-3069 from the DAEMON Tools supply chain compromise, against telecoms, universities, intergovernmental organizations, and government contractors. It was sideloaded as fake DLLs alongside legitimate software like Poedit, curl, Vim, and TightVNC, then unpacked from custom XOR-encrypted archives through shellcode loaders into a stripped-down PE format, and communicated over WebSockets with RC4-encrypted traffic and loadable modules. Defenders should hunt for spoofed DLLs such as WinSparkle.dll or libcurl.dll in unusual ProgramData paths, the hard-coded "firefox/21.0" user agent, and connections to corp.tripswithengine[.]com.

infosec.summary: Standing credentials are a liability. Every shared password or SSH key is one more thing an attacker can steal. infosec.summary: Rig Security provides an identity protection platform for agentic AI. It maps identity dependencies across providers, cloud, on-prem, network edges, and endpoints. infosec.title: FBI reportedly declares ‘cyber security incident' after hackers steal agents' personal data

ShinyHunters says it exploited an Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability and is not demanding money, but wants the bureau to correct an earlier report about its activities. The portal remains offline, and the bureau has not publicly confirmed whether the breach meets the legal threshold for a “major incident” requiring notification to Congress.

infosec.title: 24-Year-Old Arrested in Dutch Investigation Into ShinyHunters
infosec.summary: Dutch police arrested a 24-year-old Amsterdam man, identified by multiple sources as Pepijn van der Stap (aka “Umbreon”), in connection with the ShinyHunters hacking group. He previously served time for extorting over a dozen companies, earning €1.5–2.7 million, and was released in December while still facing civil suits.

The platform also supports Kubernetes deployment, GPUs, and Python, TypeScript, Go, and Rust SDKs.

devops.title: Pageindex

devops.title: Can your Postgres survive a bad query?
devops.summary: Postgres memory limits such as work_mem apply per execution node and per worker rather than per query, allowing seemingly ordinary queries to consume many times the configured amount of memory. Recursive queries can be even more dangerous because some executor hash tables cannot spill to disk, creating workloads that can exhaust memory despite conservative configuration.

devops.title: What Dependency Mocking Software Needs to Handle in a Cloud Native Architecture

Effective tools need deployment event awareness, behavior captured from real traffic rather than specs, automatic handling of non-deterministic fields, and cross-service diff visibility, with eBPF-based traffic capture cited as one approach.

devops.title: Dynamic AI Discovery & Runtime Security for AgentCore
devops.summary: Harness integrated its AI posture management and firewall with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, automatically inventorying agents, tools, and resources operating in AWS environments.

design.title: OpenAI launches Dots, its bubbly agentic avatar
design.summary: OpenAI has launched Dots, always-on personal agents powered by GPT-6 Astra that pursue user-defined goals in the background rather than staying tied to a single interface. Available to ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium users in eligible markets, Dots can be launched from ChatGPT or Codex and contacted through platforms such as Slack and Teams, with text messaging planned. Their floating, cartoon-like avatars give autonomous software a more approachable identity, while OpenAI envisions specialist Dots working together with their own tools and permissions.

design.title: You'll either love or hate the Formula E logo – and that's the whole point
design.summary: Formula E's new identity by MOX centers on a deliberately divisive logomark that combines an F and E at a 30-degree angle to convey speed and momentum. A bespoke type family based on AP Gavel expands the system with condensed italics for energy and a monospaced style for technical data, complemented by Inter for longer copy. Surge Purple, Signal Orange, and Electric Lime add a distinctive palette designed to give the championship a more expressive identity as it enters its GEN4 era.

design.title: Replit Acquires Atta to Bring AI Business Analysis into Its Platform
design.summary: Replit has acquired Atta, an AI-powered business analysis workspace, bringing its data-analysis and charting technology directly into Replit's platform. Users can upload or connect a dataset and ask Replit Agent to investigate a question or generate a visualization without writing SQL. The move reflects a broader shift toward folding business analysis into the same environment used to build and operate software.

design.title: Don't forget to design
design.summary: Design isn't something that happens after fully understanding a problem. Making sketches and prototypes is itself a way to discover what the problem really is. Rough ideas expose gaps, tensions, and requirements that research, data, and discussion alone may never reveal. An excessive focus on outcomes can discourage designers from making anything, even though reaching a good outcome often requires producing and evaluating lots of imperfect work along the way.

design.title: The Fastest Gun in UX: Why Your Team is Telling the Wrong Story
design.summary: Designers are rushing through their process to prove value through speed, but the real contest is winning stakeholder alignment, where they are both vulnerable and well positioned. The "Fastest Gun in the West" hijacks planning by anchoring early on an idea, using vague agile language, and pressuring designers to produce polished mockups that lock in unexamined assumptions while research is dismissed as slow. Since designers can't outrun someone shooting from the hip, they should use low-fidelity tools like scenario storyboards and PRFAQs to engage stakeholders on mental models and outcomes.

design.title: Skip the Tools, Make the Outcomes
design.summary: AI creates opportunities to skip traditional tools and deliver the outcomes those tools were originally designed to help people achieve. An AI-powered newsroom called Exposit discovered that users overwhelmingly preferred asking for a topic and receiving a personalized, up-to-date report instead of navigating headlines, categories, and search interfaces. This “outcome first, tool second” approach suggests a useful product design question: whether a new AI experience needs another interface at all, or can simply produce what people came for.

design.title: shadcn Marketing Blocks and Skills for AI Agents
design.summary: Initium gives your AI agent the style, strategy, blocks, and skills to generate a site that looks designed, not generated.

design.title: Design Battles
design.summary: Free online design battles in real time, with the same brief and kit for every entrant.

design.title: Product Onboarding: 100+ Real Examples, Patterns, and Best Practices
design.summary: A curated library of real product onboarding examples from Notion, Slack, Stripe, Cal, and more. Patterns, components, and the activation playbooks that move retention.

design.title: Crafting WCAG 3 for More Accessible User Experiences
design.summary: WCAG 3's September 2026 draft sets a single conformance level, called core requirements, built on WCAG 2.2's Level A and AA success criteria. Supplemental requirements, assertions, and recommended practices cover accessibility needs that can't be objectively measured or don't apply everywhere, encouraging organizations to go beyond the baseline. Tags let regulators tailor requirements to specific situations and let websites report progress toward and beyond conformance, with multiple reporting tiers built in.

design.title: Best AI Image Models 2026: Tested by Human Evaluators
design.summary: Everypixel's blind evaluation of 863 pairwise judgments across 48 commercial scenes found no universal winner among 2026's leading AI image models. GPT Image 2 showed the strongest evidence for high-precision commercial generation and controlled photorealism, though its direct comparison against real photography wasn't statistically conclusive. Qwen Image 2 suits controlled editing, Nano Banana 2 fast iteration, Nano Banana Pro consistency, Grok Imagine creative interpretation, and FLUX.2 an explore-then-finish workflow.

design.title: This Digital Artist Takes Inspiration from Old Masters and Orientalist Paintings
design.summary: Hong Kong-based illustrator Brian Yuen paints in Photoshop with a style drawn from the Old Masters and artists like Jaime Jones and Craig Mullins.

design.title: This website lets you explore nearly 30 years of Apple product colors
design.summary: Apple in Colour is an interactive archive from sheets.works that brings together 341 Apple product colors spanning nearly three decades, from the Bondi Blue iMac to recent iPhones, complete with release years and official color names.

design.title: This Advent Calendar is Filled with Design-Led Gifts
design.summary: Westwing's 2026 advent calendar comes in an oversized house-shaped box illustrated by Munich-based artist Kera Till, with 24 doors hiding home decor, tableware, and self-care pieces.

marketing.title: Adobe for Claude just got a major upgrade
marketing.summary: For the first time, Acrobat tools join Adobe's creative tools in one Adobe plugin , giving you access to 80+ pro-grade tools across imaging, design, video and documents. And now you can go beyond prompting : new interactive editors let you work hands-on with PDFs and Adobe Express designs directly inside Claude—editing text, marking up documents or fine-tuning individual design elements without leaving the conversation. Start creating and getting more done with the new Adobe for Claude plugin today. Download the new plugin in Claude here.

marketing.title: Who Gets Paid When AI Does the Shopping?
marketing.summary: AI shopping assistants could weaken marketplaces' advertising and commission economics by owning the customer relationship and sending orders directly to fulfillment providers. Amazon generated $69 billion in advertising revenue in 2025, so losing control of product discovery could threaten a major profit pool even if it keeps fulfilling orders. Platforms like Shopify and Toast have more reason to welcome agents because they can gain new sales while still earning software and payments revenue. The outcome depends on whether agents create new demand or simply reroute existing orders, since new purchases can offset lower profit per order.

marketing.title: Walmart's Collectibles Play is Showing Us Where Retail is Heading
marketing.summary: Walmart is using limited-time draws to sell scarce collectibles, including basketball cards, NeeDoh toys, and Pokémon boxes. Shoppers enter during a set window and are randomly selected instead of racing to checkout. The format creates anticipation and gives collectors a reason to discuss entry rules and results online. It shows how intentional friction can turn scarce products into experiences rather than simple transactions.

marketing.title: Money-back guarantee vs. free trial: which should your subscription app run?
marketing.summary: Asking users to pay upfront with a refund safety net lets ad campaigns optimize for real purchases instead of trial starts, giving Meta and TikTok a cleaner signal of who will pay. Few customers claim refunds, so a lower conversion rate can be offset by higher-intent subscribers. Guarantees work best in web or app-to-web funnels, since the app stores control in-app refunds.

marketing.title: How B2B Creator Marketing Builds Buyer Trust on LinkedIn
marketing.summary: B2B buyers increasingly use creators for both early research and later-stage validation. However, 80% of B2B marketers say finding credible creators is their biggest hurdle. LinkedIn recommends using Creator Marketplace to vet experts by industry, role, and audience, then amplifying their content with Thought Leader Ads or BrandLink. Thought Leader Ads deliver a 252% higher CTR than standard image ads, while BrandLink campaigns see 130% higher video completion rates than in-feed ads.

marketing.title: I went mini viral on Substack (after 9 months of crickets)
marketing.summary: The author grew her Substack from 90 to 770 subscribers in four days. She did it with a reintroduction post featuring a photo, recognizable past employers, and an honest story about leaving corporate work. She then shared subscriber numbers in real time to keep momentum going. To stay consistent, she built a Claude Skill to help create Substack notes on a set cadence, then had a VA schedule them. An email is required to read the full post.

marketing.title: How Plaid turned a TLDR placement into $382K in pipeline
marketing.summary: Plaid wanted to find a marketing channel that could deliver measurable results on a limited budget. A TLDR placement promoting its Fintech Predictions report generated 70 leads and $382K in pipeline, becoming its best-performing direct buy to date. See what worked for Plaid .

marketing.title: AI and the Agency of the Future (Webinar)
marketing.summary: Blin Kazazi and Dan Hinckley will discuss where AI fits inside an agency today. They'll cover what's changing in search and client demand, what the agency of the future looks like, and what agency owners get wrong about AI. The free webinar will take place today at 11 AM CT.

marketing.title: Jev: Decision AI for GTM
marketing.summary: Jev is a new decision model that returns labels, scores, and yes/no answers with calibrated confidence instead of generated text, making it a cheap fit for classification and routing in Clay. It connects through an HTTP API column in about 10 minutes. Keep the input state short, since extra context can lower accuracy. Add an "unclear" option and write criteria that don't overlap. Set stricter confidence thresholds for hard-to-undo actions, then gate paid enrichment and LLM writing on the result.

marketing.title: LinkedIn Is My Medium
marketing.summary: An artist created an AI-generated version of herself who is more polished and corporate than her real-world self. She uses AI to generate LinkedIn posts and images depicting promotions, luxury offices, leadership roles, and eventually a corporate scandal. The project satirizes LinkedIn's culture of self-promotion and professional visibility while questioning where performance ends and genuine professional identity begins. The irony is that the satire itself generates visibility and could make the artist more employable.

marketing.title: Why strong PMMs are struggling to land jobs (and what to do about it)
marketing.summary: Strong PMMs are struggling to land jobs because companies are hiring cautiously and looking for candidates who fit specific business needs. Job seekers experience three common roadblocks: broad positioning, forgettable interviews, and explaining experience instead of demonstrating how you would solve the company's problems. The author recommends targeting your positioning around a specific type of company and using a consultative interview approach that diagnoses the company's needs, then structures answers around Process, Situation, Action, and Result. You can also stand out by creating concrete proof of how you would solve a company's problems, such as one candidate who built an ROI calculator for a final interview and had it shared across the company.

marketing.title: Is Google Trends data inaccurate?
marketing.summary: Unrelated Google Trends queries consistently rank Cheyenne, Wyoming first, raising questions about whether non-human traffic is skewing search data.

marketing.title: Samsung TV buying journey
marketing.summary: A graphic showing a non-linear buying journey of a Samsung TV across channels and why open-web behavior matters.

marketing.title: Make product names very specific
marketing.summary: Use-specific descriptions help shoppers picture themselves using a product, which raises how useful it seems by 9.7% and purchase intent by up to 9.5%.

founders.title: Startups can get a year of Kiro Pro+. Here's how.
founders.summary: When you're pre-seed to Series A, every engineering hour counts. You can't afford to spend a week on a feature that should take a day — or ship code that breaks the moment your codebase gets real. Kiro is built exactly for this stage. Using structured specifications, clear requirements, and well-scoped task decomposition, Kiro agents have complete context on the definition of “done” before writing a single line of code. You describe what you want to build, and Kiro creates requirements, designs the architecture, sequences the tasks, and implements them. Eligible startups can apply for up to 12 months of Kiro Pro+ at no cost → Claim your free year at kiro.dev/startups Terms and Conditions apply

founders.title: Deployment Gap
founders.summary: Robotics is finally having a moment. Models are getting better, costs are coming down, and robots are logging real hours in customer facilities. However, full deployment will still take some time - even companies that publicly claim they have deployed robots often do not have them working on actual production lines. Until the technology improves, the industry will need patient capital.

founders.title: The Great AI Capital Misallocation
founders.summary: The flood of capital into AI infrastructure has left many promising startups underfunded, with investors chasing companies that can absorb huge sums quickly. AI's rapid growth benchmarks and the belief in a winner-take-all scenario drive this trend, yet hinder more traditional but solidly growing tech firms. As capital focuses on AI infrastructure, there's potential in identifying application companies ready to leverage cheaper AI tech for broader market success.

founders.title: Market to the Middle
founders.summary: Ever read a thread about your product and wondered if these people are even your customers? Tracksuit's CEO argues that online discussion overrepresents enthusiastic fans and angry critics, while ordinary buyers rarely post at all. AI recommendations can pick up those same opinions, making a vocal minority seem more representative than it is. Tracksuit compares consumer surveys with AI responses to see where perceptions differ. Before changing your positioning around a loud complaint, find out whether the customers who aren't posting share it.

founders.title: The Guerrilla Hiring Playbook
founders.summary: Leaders face challenges hiring talent in the AI-focused market, where usual tactics are less effective. Guerrilla hiring involves frontier, potential-based, and asymmetric hiring to attract trajectory-changing talent without relying on brand power. Utilizing "talent magnets" as domino hires can jumpstart recruitment by attracting follow-on candidates who define and drive expected roles and career paths.

founders.title: What TypeSafe Got Right With the Jev Launch
founders.summary: TypeSafe's Jev launch achieved rapid adoption among Vercel's paid AI teams due to its clear value and easy integration into existing workflows. A compelling demo showcased Jev's speed in making bounded decisions, outperforming competitors and highlighting its utility. The product's early success stemmed from allowing users to quickly demonstrate and share tangible outcomes, supported by strategic distribution to influential tech figures.

founders.title: Your business moves fast. So should your money.
founders.summary: Your business moves quickly. Your money should, too. Stripe Treasury brings payments and financial tools together, helping you pay vendors, send payouts, issue cards, and manage cash flow with less complexity. Build more efficient financial operations on the same platform your business already uses for payments as you continue growing. See how it works

founders.title: Meta launches Muse for Small Business with new connectors
founders.summary: Muse for Small Business enhances Muse with skills and connectors designed to help people operate and grow their companies. Users can give Muse a goal, then connect the services holding the information needed to pursue it. Muse can draw on analytics from Meta's apps and a broad set of business tools. The agent will not publish content, send messages, or spend money unless authorized.

founders.title: OpenAI DevDay 2026
founders.summary: OpenAI introduced on DevDay new models, tools, and agents to help developers build faster, take on more ambitious projects, and bring their products to more people. The company revealed new agents that can take on ongoing responsibilities and new ways for people and AI to work together. It also expanded its commitment to an open ecosystem by opening up ChatGPT as a shared surface where humans and agents can collaborate and where developers can directly launch new native experiences. There is now a new Pro 500 plan that offers 25 times the ChatGPT Plus allowance and includes access to Ultrafast.

founders.title: Modeling Software's Business Impact
founders.summary: There's no guaranteed relationship between software cost and value. While cost improvements are typically marginal and difficult, value improvements are game-changing. AI can produce a lot of work, but that doesn't mean that customers can absorb it. Businesses need to treat customer attention as the scarce resource it is and only ship the things that are truly valuable.

founders.title: The Only Reason to Raise Venture Capital
founders.summary: Founders should raise venture capital only when money is the limiting factor on growth. Treating fundraising as success can distort incentives, encourage unnecessary spending, and leave companies trapped at valuations their businesses may never justify.

founders.title: Work doesn't have to be all over the place
founders.summary: Zoom Workplace brings together meetings, docs, chat, and more with ZoomMate built in. Simplify how your team works — everything in one place.. $20 off annual plans with code: TLDRZWP20* *Valid on annual plans only. One-time discount. Offer expires 9/22/27.

founders.title: Who Gets Paid When AI Does the Shopping?
founders.summary: AI shopping agents could capture the customer relationship without owning fulfillment, shifting economics away from marketplaces' ads and commissions.

founders.title: How GPU Prices Can Double While AI Gets Cheaper
founders.summary: GPU prices have surged from $4.40 to $8.08 per GPU-hour due to rising data center construction costs.

founders.title: Fire and Ice
founders.summary: Is your team better at getting excited about the next project or finishing the current one?

crypto.title: Coinbase Receives CFTC Approval as Derivatives Clearing Organization
crypto.summary: Coinbase received CFTC approval to operate as a Derivatives Clearing Organization (DCO), adding clearinghouse status to its existing exchange and broker licenses to form a vertically integrated regulated derivatives stack. The approval order restricts Coinbase to fully collateralized products, with leverage expected via a future amendment. The clearinghouse designation positions Coinbase to back permissioned institutional derivatives markets through Hyperliquid's HIP-3 framework, which allows licensed partners to operate compliant perp trading venues. Coinbase becomes the second major crypto exchange after Kraken to hold CFTC-regulated clearing capabilities, completing the exchange-broker-clearinghouse triad that institutional counterparties require for compliant derivatives exposure.

crypto.title: SEC Clarifies Decentralized Token Buybacks Are Not Investment Contracts
crypto.summary: The SEC updated its crypto FAQ to clarify that decentralized token buyback programs, where no central party is involved, do not constitute investment contracts under the Howey test. The revision followed feedback from a16z Crypto General Counsel Miles Jennings, who warned that prior wording could cause a buyback announcement alone to trigger securities classification for the issuer. The broader September 25 FAQ batch also addressed how the SEC's March digital assets interpretive release applies to token functionality and staking receipt tokens, including a clarification that services to maintain or grow a functional network do not qualify as "essential managerial efforts" under Howey. The FAQs carry no legal force as staff views, but the responsive revision gives DeFi protocols running on-chain buyback mechanisms clearer grounds to structure those programs without securities registration concerns.

crypto.title: Proof Launches Conditionals Exchange: Event-Contingent Crypto Derivatives
crypto.summary: Proof is building a derivatives exchange around a new instrument class called Conditionals, which price assets contingent on specific events and settle to the underlying position if the condition is met or revert to zero PnL if not. The design addresses a gap between prediction markets and spot/perp trading: existing event markets tell traders whether something happens but do not reveal what an asset is worth if that event occurs. US equities generated over 60% of their excess returns on roughly 13% of trading days tied to scheduled macro announcements, a figure Proof cites to frame the scale of event-conditional demand that current instruments leave unmet. The protocol runs on testnet after a June v0 Challenge with 500+ paper-trading participants, with a capped real-money Mainnet Private Alpha rolling out shortly.

crypto.title: Chainlink Launches CCIP 2.0 With Ethlabs FCR, Cutting Cross-Chain Confirmations 30x
crypto.summary: Chainlink launched CCIP 2.0 on September 28, adding Cross-Chain Verifiers (CCVs) that let enterprises attach custom security checks before destination-chain execution, built-in KYC, AML, and sanctions screening on every transaction, AWS and Google Cloud deployment kits, and additive verification from Infosys, Nethermind, and Deutsche Börse's Crypto Finance, bringing the protocol's secured token value above $84 billion. Ethlabs integrated its Fast Confirmation Rule (FCR) with CCIP 2.0, drawing quick-action signals from Ethereum's existing validator consensus to drop cross-chain confirmation times from approximately 13 minutes to 12-24 seconds (30x faster) without new economic assumptions or additional infrastructure. The combined update targets institutional RWA issuers and tokenized asset distributors requiring compliance enforcement and sub-30-second settlement across chains.

crypto.title: Do Bitcoin Maxis Have A Zcash Answer?
crypto.summary: "Shielded Bitcoin" is a metaprotocol that ports Zcash's encrypted-note, ZK-proof privacy architecture to Bitcoin L1 via OP_RETURN data envelopes, requiring no soft fork or sidechain. The design defers trustless peg-in/peg-out to a future paper, leaving the bridge problem open, and depends on Bitcoin Core v30's relaxed OP_RETURN relay policy. The paper arrives as ZEC has climbed ~2,500% over the past year to a ~$26B market cap (ranked #9), with Grayscale's ZCSH ETF drawing $250M+ in net inflows since August 25 and public ZEC holdings disclosed by Paradigm co-founder Matt Huang and Multicoin. Citrea (Galaxy Ventures) acquired privacy wallet Crest to target the same problem on Bitcoin L2, while NEAR Protocol rolled out confidential perps and limit orders by default, with both teams citing AI-powered surveillance tools, including LLMs re-identifying pseudonymous users, as the core demand driver.

crypto.title: Citi Partners With Coinbase for Institutional Stablecoin Payments
crypto.summary: Citi, with $2.8T in assets and a payment network spanning 94 markets and 300+ clearing systems, has partnered with Coinbase to offer institutional clients stablecoin payment services covering fiat-to-stablecoin conversion, onchain transfers, and stablecoin-to-fiat settlement. The arrangement layers Coinbase's crypto custody and $246B asset platform onto Citi's regulated banking rails, giving institutional clients a compliant on/off ramp to stablecoin flows without depending on crypto-native intermediaries. The deal extends one of the largest global correspondent banking networks to onchain settlement, putting stablecoin payment reach within regulated multicurrency infrastructure that institutional counterparties already operate inside. Citi also projects stablecoin issuance will reach $1.9T by 2030 in its base case, indicating the bank is building this infrastructure ahead of anticipated supply growth rather than in response to it.

crypto.title: Aave is turning into a credit layer as tokenized stocks become collateral
crypto.summary: Aave increasingly looks less like a lending protocol and more like a credit layer, as tokenized stocks cross $3.5 billion in market cap and Coinbase's tokenized stocks become productive collateral on Aave. Stocks, tokenized funds, custodied BTC and ETH, RWAs, and crypto collateral are all increasingly being originated through Aave, while on the borrower side, Coinbase can lend against tokenized equities, institutions can access stablecoin credit, fintechs can embed Aave liquidity, and banks may eventually launch their own fronts for the Aave app, calling the addressable market for Aave closer to credit broadly than DeFi lending specifically.

crypto.title: Flex explains how its 5% cashback tier for founders actually works
crypto.summary: In Flex's new Elite tier, personal cashback starts at 3% and rises based on business deposits kept with Flex. $250,000 in deposits unlocks 4% cashback, and $1 million or more unlocks 5%. Flex funds the higher rewards from revenue generated on business deposits. Several $100 million-plus companies have already switched from competitors because of the structure, a rare direct link between a business banking relationship and personal rewards.

crypto.title: EtherFi's Crypto Card now drives nearly 60% of its revenue
crypto.summary: EtherFi's own numbers show last week's $868,000 in revenue came mostly from its Crypto Card ($507,000), followed by staking ($266,000), Liquid vaults ($58,000), borrowing ($28,000), and swaps ($9,000).

crypto.title: Top 10 crypto card projects by total spend
crypto.summary: Top 10 crypto card projects by cumulative user spend are RedotPay, EtherFi Cash, KAST, Katra, Gnosis Pay, Tria, Karta Personal, Kolo, Wirex One, and MetaMask.

crypto.title: Institutional crypto capital stayed sticky through the drawdown
crypto.summary: A Bitwise survey of 15 of the world's largest institutions on their crypto allocations demonstrated that none of the institutions cut exposure during a 50% drawdown, and some added to positions.

crypto.title: EUR rail tests across Krak, EtherFi Cash, Anodos, and Plasma One
crypto.summary: Krak offered instant EUR transfers with no conversion, a personal IBAN, and zero deposit fee.

it.title: NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform: A Reference for Continuous In-Silicon Agent Monitoring
it.summary: NVIDIA's Open Agent Safety Platform pairs OpenShell, an Apache 2.0 sandboxed runtime that turns operator instructions into verifiable file, network, tool, and credential policies, with Sentry, a monitor that runs on BlueField-4 DPUs. In Vera Rubin PODs, the DPU sits on the node's only path to the model, so it can enforce policy at line speed outside the agent's reach. NVIDIA's argument is that agents can't be trusted to govern themselves, so safety controls have to sit below them in hardware.

it.title: Microsoft's Copilot super app comes with a meter attached
it.summary: Microsoft is splitting Copilot pricing in two. A per-user subscription still covers "Everyday AI" in Office apps, while agentic features like Cowork, Code, Autopilot, and frontier models are billed by usage on top of the seat. Admins get spending caps and alerts, but budgets that were fixed per head now have to absorb costs from agents that run without a user prompting them.

it.title: Test-driving Jev on a security task: identity resolution
it.summary: Vincenzo Iozzo tested Jev, a specialized classification model, on matching accounts across systems to the same person in five real organizations. Jev scored 0.948 F1 on large orgs at $0.62 per 1,000 accounts, beating Claude Haiku 4.5 (0.894 F1, 19x the cost) and Sonnet 5 (0.911 F1, 47x the cost) at roughly a tenth of their latency. His conclusion is that small calibrated models beat prompted frontier LLMs on bounded, high-volume security classification.

it.title: What happens when the cloud blows up?
it.summary: Missile and drone strikes during the March 2026 Iran conflict hit AWS facilities in the UAE and Bahrain. AWS says the damage exceeded what its multi-AZ design can withstand, and restoration isn't expected until early 2027. The piece argues that availability zones don't fail independently when a whole region is physically attacked, and that continuity plans should account for that.

it.title: Microsoft Announces General Availability Of WSLC: Linux Containers On Windows
it.summary: WSLC, Microsoft's native way to run Linux containers on Windows, is now generally available through a new wslc.exe command. Each session gets its own storage VHD, stronger isolation, and a new networking model compared with standard WSL. The code is open source in the microsoft/wsl GitHub repository.

it.title: Introducing Threat Signals: agentic skills for open-source threat intelligence, free for every Cloudflare account
it.summary: Cloudflare's Threat Signals uses agentic skills to read open-source threat reports from RSS feeds, summarize them, extract indicators of compromise, and tag threats. It then links those findings to WAF rules while keeping the context of the original source. Cloudflare also made its Threat Events Platform free for every account, with paid tiers for more feeds, proprietary data, and custom skills.

it.title: Building a post-quantum certificate authority with Merkle Tree Certificates
it.summary: Cloudflare is becoming a certificate authority that issues Merkle Tree Certificates for free, and it is targeting Chrome's quantum-resistant root store in early 2027. Post-quantum signatures are about 40x larger than classical ones, so MTCs batch many certificates under a single CA signature and build transparency logging into issuance. In a Chrome experiment covering 50% of Beta users, the lightweight MTC format already made handshakes 9% faster.

it.title: Google seemingly confirms plans to kill ChromeOS in 2034
it.summary: A new Google support page for enterprise and education customers says ChromeOS support will continue through mid-2034, and newer Chromebooks will be migrated to the Android-based Googlebook OS. This is a problem for schools, because Googlebooks start at $899 and won't have comparable management tools for a year or more.

it.title: Agent Memory Is a Search Problem, Not a Storage Problem
it.summary: Tiger Data skipped fact extraction, knowledge graphs, and memory managers.

it.title: How to roll out Genie One: A step-by-step enterprise playbook
it.summary: Databricks published a four-phase rollout plan for Genie One, its AI coworker for business data questions.

it.title: A Data Center Is a Dependency Graph Before It Is a Building
it.summary: A finished hyperscale region can sit idle for 6 to 12 months because hundreds of interdependent services have to come up in the right order, and some depend on each other, such as DNS relying on inventory while inventory relies on DNS.

hardware.title: Starship Reaches Orbit for the First Time on Flight 14, Deploys 26 Next-Gen Starlink Satellites
hardware.summary: Starship's 14th test flight reached orbit for the first time on Monday, despite one engine shutting down unexpectedly mid-flight, deploying 26 next-generation Starlink V3 satellites one by one from a Pez-dispenser-style mechanism at roughly 269km altitude before the mission ended early. Each Starship can now carry about 60 Starlink V3 satellites, roughly 20 times the capacity of a Falcon 9 launch, and the new satellites offer around 10x the downlink and 22x the uplink capacity of the previous V2 generation, capability SpaceX needs to support Musk's stated goal of Starlink eventually carrying a majority of the world's internet traffic.

hardware.title: Nvidia Puts Agent Monitoring Directly on the BlueField-4 DPU, Off the Host an Agent Could Compromise
hardware.summary: Nvidia's Open Agent Safety Platform pairs OpenShell, a sandboxed runtime running on its Vera CPU, with Sentry, a monitoring layer that runs in silicon on the BlueField-4 DPU rather than on the same host as the agent it's watching. The architectural bet is physical separation as a security property: in a Vera Rubin POD, each compute tray's BlueField-4 sits on the node's only path to the model, meaning every agent "thought" has to pass through that chip, giving it both the best observation point and a hardware kill switch, isolated from the host and beyond the agent's own reach even if the host itself gets compromised.

hardware.title: VSMC Opens First 300mm Fab in Singapore, VIS-NXP Joint Venture Hits 99%+ Yields
hardware.summary: VisionPower Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, a joint venture between Vanguard International Semiconductor and NXP, opened its first 300mm wafer fab in Tampines, Singapore, completed in just 22 months and now in risk production after its first sample lot cleared yields above 99%. The fab targets mature nodes between 130nm and 40nm for power management, mixed-signal, analog, and interposer chips serving automotive, industrial, consumer, mobile, and HPC customers, with volume manufacturing starting Q1 2027 and full capacity, roughly 44,000 wafers a month and 1,600 jobs, targeted by 2029.

hardware.title: Tesla's Optimus Hands Still Aren't Reliable Enough for Mass Production, Report Says
hardware.summary: Tesla ramped Optimus production from a few dozen units in Q2 to several hundred a week last month, but the company is hitting real engineering roadblocks on the path to its 20,000-units-a-week target for year-end. Most units built so far aren't shipping to customers at all, instead staying in-house for testing and data collection, and are still confined to simple, repetitive tasks rather than functioning as general-purpose machines. The core problem is durability and reliable assembly of the hands, a struggle Tesla has reportedly wrestled with for over a year, and rather than relying on touch sensors built directly into the hand itself, the company is now developing a hot-swappable "sensing glove" as a workaround.

hardware.title: The Flying Car Company Soaring Toward Wall Street
hardware.summary: After nearly a decade of R&D, Doroni unveiled a showroom model of its H1-X flying car. Morgan Stanley projects a $9T market by 2050. First deliveries are targeted for 2028. Invest at $3.30/share before 10/23

hardware.title: New ROS 2 Node Definition Language Framework
hardware.summary: Announced at ROSCon Global 2026 in Toronto, the NODL framework provides a metadata language to formally describe the ROS interface of a robotic node, including its topics, parameters, services, and actions. It allows developer tools to validate configuration layouts, auto-generate boilerplate code, and create automated testing setups directly from declarative node specifications. For anyone designing embedded control software or complex sensor integrations, this tool offers a standardized way to ensure subsystem nodes communicate reliably without manual, error-prone integration checks.

hardware.title: AMD Acquires World Labs
hardware.summary: AMD has agreed to acquire World Labs, a startup specializing in spatial intelligence and deep learning models designed to understand the physical three-dimensional world. This merger aims to build an open, end-to-end AI ecosystem by combining frontier physical intelligence research directly with high-performance silicon development. This acquisition is exceptionally relevant to those building physical machines because it bridges the gap between hardware acceleration and the spatial awareness foundation models required for next-generation robotic manipulation and navigation.

hardware.title: VAST Data's DataEnclave Uses Nvidia Confidential Computing to Run AI Models Directly Inside Locked-Down Data
hardware.summary: VAST Data unveiled DataEnclave, a confidential AI runtime built on NVIDIA Confidential Computing, aimed at industries like finance, healthcare, and government where sensitive data can't leave tightly controlled environments and outside AI models normally can't reach it. The system creates hardware-isolated secure enclaves using CPU and GPU trusted execution environments, requiring cryptographic attestation that verifies the environment and its enforced policy before any decryption key is released, so proprietary model weights and sensitive customer data get decrypted only inside a verified enclave and stay encrypted in both CPU and GPU memory while processing, invisible even to the infrastructure operator running the hardware.

hardware.title: TSMC's 2024 $1T-by-2030 Forecast Was Already $700B Too Low
hardware.summary: At TSMC's OIP North America symposium, VP Sajiv Dalal now projects the semiconductor industry hitting roughly $1.7 trillion by year-end, with AI alone crossing $1 trillion, dwarfing TSMC's own "aggressive" 2024 forecast of $1 trillion for the whole industry by 2030. TSMC's revenue is up 53.3% year-over-year through August, and new tape-outs have quadrupled across the N5, N3, and N2 nodes, with N2 seeing an especially sharp acceleration in new chip designs.

hardware.title: Mastering the ROS RMW Workshop
hardware.summary: This repository contains the training materials, benchmarks, and hands-on exercises for a technical workshop focused on tuning ROS 2 middleware performance.

hardware.title: Samsung Electro-Mechanics Invests 6.78 Trillion Won in AI Chip Package Substrates
hardware.summary: Samsung Electro-Mechanics is investing a combined 6.78 trillion won ($4.9 billion) to expand FC-BGA substrate production, 4.27 trillion won for a new plant at its Sejong site, and 2.51 trillion won for its Vietnam subsidiary, marking the company's largest-ever investment in a single product.

hardware.title: CERN Releases "colibri," a Vendor-Independent VHDL Common Library for FPGAs
hardware.summary: CERN's EP department released colibri, a VHDL common library built up over four years after gateware designers found themselves relying on homebrew tools scattered across FPGAs from multiple vendors.

hardware.title: Enterprise Red Hat Linux Support for ROS 2
hardware.summary: Red Hat Enterprise Linux has officially achieved Tier 1 support status in the Robot Operating System 2 development ecosystem, beginning with the Rolling Ridley release.
